- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.22), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 18-day mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above recent high.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates 30d mean; adjust downward by 1–3% for 10–15d horizon.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model often underestimates mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for 15–30d.
- If 18-day history shows strong downward momentum, model tends to ignore it; increase downward bias by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is weak.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome deviates >3% from 18d mean, adjust forecast to align with 18d mean ± 1.5% unless sentiment strongly supports divergence.
